senses.title: Relating to molecules
senses.titleCN: 分子的：与分子这一实体有关
senses.definition: relating to molecules as the smallest units of a substance that keep its chemical identity
senses.definitionCN: 指与分子有关的；分子是保持物质化学性质的最小单元
senses.example: The two samples differ only at the molecular level.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个样本只在分子层面有所不同。
senses.why: Molecule plus -ar makes a relating adjective, as in similar or regular: molecular means 'of a molecule'. The suffix points at the entity, not at the science.
senses.whyCN: molecule 加 -ar 构成关系形容词，如同 similar、regular：molecular 意为「分子的」。词尾指向这个实体，而不是这门学科。

senses.title: At the molecular level: a scale of description
senses.titleCN: 分子层面的：一种描述尺度
senses.definition: describing a level of explanation that deals with molecules rather than with visible objects or with atoms
senses.definitionCN: 指在分子这一尺度上解释，而不是在可见物体或原子的尺度上解释
senses.example: The disease has a molecular explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病有一个分子层面的解释。
senses.why: Once a level of description is named, the adjective can mark it. Between the atom and the cell sits the molecule, and molecular names everything that happens there.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某一描述层级被命名，这个形容词就能标记它。原子与细胞之间是分子，凡发生在这一层的事都叫 molecular。

senses.title: Of molecular structure: how atoms are arranged
senses.titleCN: 分子结构的：原子如何排布
senses.definition: relating to the arrangement of atoms within a molecule and the bonds between them
senses.definitionCN: 指分子内部原子的排布以及它们之间的化学键
senses.example: The drug's molecular structure was mapped in detail.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药的分子结构被详细绘制出来。
senses.why: Structure is what the molecule has instead of a shape you can see. The adjective marks the internal architecture that determines how the substance behaves.
senses.whyCN: 分子拥有的是结构，而不是看得见的形状。这个形容词标记决定物质行为的内部构造。

senses.title: Of molecular biology: the field that works at this level
senses.titleCN: 分子生物学的：在这一层面工作的学科
senses.definition: relating to the branch of biology that studies the molecules that carry and express genetic information
senses.definitionCN: 指研究承载与表达遗传信息的分子的生物学分支
senses.example: Molecular biology transformed how cells are understood.
senses.exampleCN: 分子生物学改变了人们对细胞的理解。
senses.why: A field is named by the level it works at. Molecular biology studies life through its molecules, and the adjective simply attaches the field's name to its noun.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科以它工作的层级来命名。分子生物学通过分子研究生命，而这个形容词只是把学科名称接到名词上。

senses.title: Of molecular weight and formula
senses.definition: relating to values calculated from a molecule's composition, such as its formula and its weight
senses.definitionCN: 指由分子的组成计算出的数值，如分子式与分子量
senses.example: Molecular weight is expressed in daltons.
senses.exampleCN: 分子量用道尔顿表示。
senses.why: A molecule has a countable composition: so many atoms of each kind. The adjective therefore also covers the numbers derived from that composition.
senses.whyCN: 分子的组成是可数的：每类原子各有多少个。因此这个形容词也覆盖由该组成推导出的数值。

senses.title: Molecular scale: extremely small
senses.definition: describing sizes, devices or effects on the scale of molecules, far below the visible
senses.definitionCN: 指在分子尺度上的尺寸、器件或效应，远小于肉眼可见
senses.example: Molecular machines move a few nanometres at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 分子机器每次只移动几纳米。
senses.why: Here the adjective works like a unit of size. It says that the thing operates at the scale where molecules, not millimetres, are the natural measure.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词相当于一种尺寸单位。它说明该事物运作的尺度上，天然的单位是分子，而不是毫米。

senses.title: Of molecular genetics: inheritance at this level
senses.titleCN: 分子遗传学的：在这一层面研究遗传
senses.definition: relating to the study of inheritance through the structure and activity of DNA and related molecules
senses.definitionCN: 指通过 DNA（脱氧核糖核酸）及相关分子的结构与活动来研究遗传
senses.example: Molecular genetics identified the mutation.
senses.exampleCN: 分子遗传学定位到了这个突变。
senses.why: Genetics used to be about breeding ratios; molecular genetics is about the material. The adjective marks the shift from pattern to mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学过去关心繁育比例，分子遗传学关心物质本身。这个形容词标记了从模式到机制的转变。

senses.title: Of molecular medicine: treatment aimed at molecules
senses.titleCN: 分子医学的：把治疗对准分子
senses.definition: relating to medicine that diagnoses or treats disease by acting on specific molecules
senses.definitionCN: 指通过作用于特定分子来诊断或治疗疾病的医学
senses.example: Molecular medicine targets the faulty protein directly.
senses.exampleCN: 分子医学直接针对那个出错的蛋白。
senses.why: Medicine adds the adjective when the target of treatment is a molecule rather than an organ. The word marks precision at the smallest working scale.
senses.whyCN: 当治疗针对的是分子而非器官时，医学就在前面加上这个形容词。这个词标记的是最小工作尺度上的精确性。

intro.en: Molecular is molecule plus -ar, the relating suffix seen in similar and regular. Molecule goes back through French molécule to Latin molecula, a diminutive of moles 'mass, heap, massive structure'. The adjective is recorded in the 19th century, once chemistry had fixed what a molecule is. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: molecular 是 molecule 加 -ar，这个关系后缀也见于 similar 与 regular。molecule 经法语 molécule 追溯到拉丁语 molecula，后者是 moles「块体、堆、庞大结构」的指小形式。该形容词在 19 世纪见于记载，当时化学已确定分子的含义。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Molecular biology, molecular genetics and molecular medicine become names of whole fields.
items.cn: 分子生物学、分子遗传学与分子医学成为整门学科的名称。

items.en: English molecular is recorded, formed on molecule with -ar once the chemical concept was established.
items.cn: 英语 molecular 见于记载，在化学概念确立后由 molecule 加 -ar 构成。

items.en: French molécule supplies the immediate source, a learned coinage from the Latin diminutive molecula.
items.cn: 法语 molécule 是直接来源，它是从拉丁指小形式 molecula 造出的学术词。

items.en: molecula is a diminutive of moles 'mass, heap', so a molecule was first a small mass rather than a bonded group of atoms.
items.cn: molecula 是 moles「块体、堆」的指小形式，因此 molecule 最初指一小团物质，而不是成键的原子团。

items.en: The further origin of moles is of uncertain origin; it is not securely traced to a single reconstructed root.
items.cn: moles 的更早来源不确定，未能可靠地追溯到某一个重构词根。

note.en: The first group separates two homographs and one false neighbour from the family; the second compares adjectives of very small scale.
note.cn: 第一组把两个同形异义词与一个假邻居从词族中分出来；第二组比较表示极小尺度的形容词。

entries.definition: a grinding tooth, or a concentration per mole. The tooth sense comes from Latin mola 'millstone', and the chemistry sense from mole, so neither is a relative of molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 磨牙，或指每摩尔的浓度。牙齿义出自拉丁语 mola「磨石」，化学义出自 mole，两者都不是 molecule 的同族词。

entries.definition: The animal comes from Germanic roots and the unit of chemical amount is shortened from molecule. The two spell the same but share no history.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物时出自日耳曼词根；指化学物质的量单位时则是 molecule 的缩略。两者拼写相同，却没有共同的历史。

entries.definition: the smallest unit of a substance that keeps its chemical identity. The adjective molecular adds only the relating suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 保持物质化学性质的最小单元。形容词 molecular 只加了一个关系后缀。

entries.definition: relating to atoms, the units below molecules. Atomic work goes one level deeper than molecular work.
entries.definitionCN: 与原子有关的，原子在分子之下。原子层面的工作比分子层面的工作再深一层。

entries.definition: consisting of small separate particles, especially in air or water. It names bits of matter, not chemically bonded units.
entries.definitionCN: 由细小颗粒构成的，尤指空气或水中的颗粒。它指物质的碎粒，而不是化学成键的单元。

entries.definition: too small to be seen with an ordinary microscope. It describes size alone, with no claim about chemical structure.
entries.definitionCN: 小到普通显微镜看不见。它只描述大小，不对化学结构作任何主张。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: molecule plus -ar gives molecular, exactly as similar comes from simil- plus -ar.
normal.cn: molecule 加 -ar 得到 molecular，正如 similar 由 simil- 加 -ar 而来。

normal.en: The -cule in molecule is a Latin diminutive, so the word began as 'a little mass'.
normal.cn: molecule 里的 -cule 是拉丁指小成分，所以这个词最初是「一小团物质」。

normal.en: Molar the tooth comes from mola 'millstone' and is not a relative; molar the concentration comes from mole.
normal.cn: 指牙齿的 molar 出自 mola「磨石」，并非同族；指浓度的 molar 则出自 mole。

normal.en: Every molecular phrase names a level: structure, weight, biology, genetics, medicine.
normal.cn: 每个 molecular 短语都命名一个层级：结构、重量、生物学、遗传学、医学。

normal.en: macromolecule and bimolecular show how the family grows: macro- for large, bi- for two.
normal.cn: macromolecule 与 bimolecular 显示这个词族如何生长：macro- 表大，bi- 表二。

abstract.en: Picture zooming into sugar until the crystal becomes a crowd of small joined shapes.
abstract.cn: 想象不断放大糖粒，直到晶体变成一大群相连的小形状。

abstract.en: The molecular level is the workshop where chemistry explains what the eye cannot see.
abstract.cn: 分子层面就是化学解释肉眼所不见之物的那间作坊。

abstract.en: The word always lowers the scale of the question rather than changing the question.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是把问题的尺度放低，而不改变问题本身。

examples.en: Molecular evidence placed the species in a different family.
examples.cn: 分子层面的证据把这个物种归入了另一个科。

examples.en: The lab studies molecular changes during freezing.
examples.cn: 这个实验室研究冷冻过程中的分子变化。

examples.en: Molecular weight affects how fast the substance diffuses.
examples.cn: 分子量影响这种物质扩散的快慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫乐扣了」——莫要乐得把扣子扣错，先看清分子怎么连的 → molecular 分子的

root: 拉丁语 moles「块体、堆」→ 指小形式 molecula「一小团物质」→ 法语 molécule → 英语 molecule；加 -ar（关系形容词后缀）→ molecular。核心是「把尺度降到分子这一层去看」。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a scale small enough that atoms appear as joined shapes. What changes is the question asked at that scale — what a molecule is, at which level we explain, how it is built, which field studies it, what numbers describe it, how small it is, how inheritance works there, or how medicine acts there.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一个尺度，小到原子显现为相连的形状。变化的只是在该尺度上问什么——分子是什么、我们在哪一层解释、它怎么搭建、哪门学科研究它、用哪些数字描述它、它有多小、遗传在此如何运作，还是医学如何在此起作用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grain of sugar magnified until two spheres hang from a spring.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒糖被放大，直到看见两个小球被一根弹簧连着。

branches.en: THE ENTITY AND ITS LEVEL: molecular names the molecule and also the layer of explanation where it sits.
branches.cn: 实体及其层级：molecular 既指分子，也指分子所处的解释层级。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AND NUMBER: structure says how atoms are joined, formula and weight say how many of each.
branches.cn: 排布与数字：结构说明原子如何相连，分子式与分子量说明各有几个。

branches.en: THE FIELDS: biology and genetics work at this level, and their names carry the adjective.
branches.cn: 学科：生物学与遗传学在这一层面工作，其名称带着这个形容词。

branches.en: THE SCALE ITSELF: devices and effects measured in nanometres are molecular in size.
branches.cn: 尺度本身：以纳米计的器件与效应，在大小上是分子级的。

branches.en: MEDICINE AT THE TARGET: treatment aims at a specific molecule instead of an organ.
branches.cn: 对准靶点的医学：治疗针对特定分子，而不是器官。

intro.en: Molecular is molecule plus -ar. The suffix -ar, from Latin -aris, makes a relating adjective; molecule itself is a diminutive in -cule from Latin moles.
intro.cn: molecular 是 molecule 加 -ar。后缀 -ar 出自拉丁语 -aris，构成关系形容词；molecule 本身则是拉丁语 moles 加 -cule 的指小形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is moles 'mass, heap, massive structure'. Its diminutive molecula gives molecule, and moles also underlies demolish and mole as a breakwater.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 moles「块体、堆、庞大结构」。其指小形式 molecula 给出 molecule，moles 还支撑 demolish 与作防波堤解的 mole。

items.example: Molecular structure decides the drug's effect.
items.exampleCN: 分子结构决定药效。

items.meaningCN: 保持化学性质的最小单元
items.example: A water molecule has three atoms.
items.exampleCN: 一个水分子有三个原子。

items.example: The two oils are molecularly similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两种油在分子层面相似。

items.meaning: the state of being molecular; in chemistry, the number of molecules reacting
items.meaningCN: 分子性；（化学）反应分子数
items.example: The reaction's molecularity is two.
items.exampleCN: 这个反应的分子数是二。

items.meaning: a very large molecule such as a protein
items.example: Proteins are macromolecules built from amino acids.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质是由氨基酸构成的大分子。

items.meaning: involving two molecules in a reaction step
items.meaningCN: 双分子的（一步反应涉及两个分子）
items.example: The step is bimolecular.
items.exampleCN: 这一步是双分子反应。

items.meaningCN: 摩尔（物质的量单位，由 molecule 缩略而来）
items.example: One mole contains Avogadro's number of particles.
items.exampleCN: 一摩尔含有阿伏伽德罗常数个粒子。

items.example: Molar concentration is written in mol per litre.
items.exampleCN: 摩尔浓度以每升摩尔数表示。

items.meaningCN: 拆除；推倒（de- 表示向下，moliri 出自 moles）
items.example: They demolished the old mill.
items.exampleCN: 他们拆掉了那座旧磨坊。

items.structure: Latin moles used for a massive barrier
items.meaning: a stone breakwater built out into the sea
items.meaningCN: 防波堤（原义为庞大的堆体）
items.example: The harbour mole protects the boats.
items.exampleCN: 港口的防波堤保护着船只。

latinEntries.meaning: a mass, a heap, a massive structure

definition_zh: 分子；微粒；生物大分子；单分子；气体或液体中的独立单元；极少量；聚合物的重复单元；微小成分
definition_en: the smallest unit of a substance that keeps its chemical identity, consisting of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds
core_image: 两个氧原子被一条看不见的弹簧拉住，独自成团地飘在空气里
scene: 两个氧原子被看不见的键牵在一起漂移，这样一个整体就是分子。Two oxygen atoms held together by an invisible bond drift as one group: that group is a molecule.
sceneCN: 这里 molecule 是「分子」（第 1 个义项：化学中的最小独立单元）；句意：两个氧原子被一条看不见的键拉在一起，作为一个整体在空气中漂移，这个整体就是分子。图中可辨识物件：两个相连的氧原子模型、代表化学键的虚线、空气背景中的其它分子、比例标尺；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 分子；微粒；极小量

senses.title: The chemical unit: atoms bonded into one group
senses.titleCN: 化学分子：原子成键组成的整体
senses.definition: the smallest unit of a substance that keeps its chemical identity, made of atoms held together by chemical bonds
senses.definitionCN: 保持物质化学性质的最小单元，由化学键连接的原子组成
senses.example: A water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
senses.exampleCN: 一个水分子含两个氢原子和一个氧原子。
senses.why: Molecule began as Latin molecula, 'a little mass'. Chemistry narrowed it to the smallest group of bonded atoms that still behaves as the substance, so the word moved from 'small lump' to 'bonded unit'.
senses.whyCN: molecule 最初是拉丁语 molecula「一小团物质」。化学把它收窄为仍然表现为该物质的最小成键原子团，于是词义从「小团块」转成「成键单元」。

senses.title: A tiny particle of matter
senses.definition: a very small particle of a substance, considered without regard to its internal bonds
senses.definitionCN: 物质中极小的颗粒，不考虑其内部成键情况
senses.example: Dust molecules coated the mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘微粒覆盖了镜面。
senses.why: The older, looser sense survives in ordinary speech, where any very small piece of matter may be called a molecule. Here the word means size, not chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 较旧、较松的义项在日常语言中留存，任何极小的物质碎屑都可能被称为 molecule。此处词义指的是大小，而不是化学。

senses.title: Biological macromolecule: proteins, DNA, starch
senses.titleCN: 生物大分子：蛋白质、DNA、淀粉
senses.definition: a very large molecule built from many repeating units, especially one found in living things
senses.definitionCN: 由许多重复单元构成的极大分子，尤指存在于生物体中的
senses.example: Each cell contains thousands of protein molecules.
senses.exampleCN: 每个细胞含有数千个蛋白质分子。
senses.why: Biology called its long chains molecules because they are bonded units, then added macro- when the size became the point. The base word keeps its chemical sense throughout.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把长链称为 molecule，因为它们就是成键单元；当大小成为重点时，又加上 macro-。词基本身始终保留化学义。

senses.title: Single-molecule work: studying one at a time
senses.titleCN: 单分子：一次只研究一个
senses.definition: in research, one individual molecule examined or manipulated on its own rather than in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 研究中指被单独观测或操作的那一个分子，而不是整批
senses.example: Single-molecule imaging revealed the folding steps.
senses.exampleCN: 单分子成像揭示了折叠的各个步骤。
senses.why: When instruments became sharp enough, the word needed a countable singular. Single-molecule marks the shift from averaging a crowd to watching one individual.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器足够精细时，这个词需要一个可数的单数形式。single-molecule 标记了从对一群分子取平均，转为观察单个分子的转变。

senses.title: The independent unit in a gas or liquid
senses.titleCN: 气体或液体中的独立单元
senses.definition: the separate unit that moves independently in a gas or solution, as opposed to a continuous network
senses.definitionCN: 在气体或溶液中独立运动的单元，与连续网络相对
senses.example: Gas molecules collide millions of times each second.
senses.exampleCN: 气体分子每秒碰撞数百万次。
senses.why: Kinetic theory needs a unit that travels freely. A molecule is exactly that: a bonded group small enough to move as one body through a fluid.
senses.whyCN: 动理论需要一个能自由行进的单元。分子正合适：那是一个小到能作为一个整体在流体中运动的成键原子团。

senses.title: A trace: a molecule of something
senses.definition: an extremely small amount of something, used in phrases such as not a molecule of truth
senses.definitionCN: 极少的量，用在 not a molecule of truth（一点真相也没有）一类的说法中
senses.example: There is not a molecule of evidence for that claim.
senses.exampleCN: 那个主张连一丝证据都没有。
senses.why: Because a molecule is invisibly small, the word can mean 'the least possible amount'. The metaphor borrows the chemist's smallest unit for the smallest imaginable trace.
senses.whyCN: 因为分子小到不可见，这个词可以表示「可能的最少量」。这一比喻借化学家的最小单位，指想象所及的最微小痕迹。

senses.title: The repeating unit of a polymer
senses.definition: in polymer chemistry, the repeating structural unit from which a long chain is built
senses.definitionCN: 高分子化学中指构成长链的重复结构单元
senses.example: Each molecule in the chain repeats the same pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 链中的每个单元重复着同一模式。
senses.why: Here the word names the brick rather than the wall. Polymer science counts how many molecule units are joined, so molecule marks the unit of repetition.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指的是砖，而不是墙。高分子科学要数有多少个分子单元被连起来，因此 molecule 标记的是重复单位。

senses.title: A minute element of a larger thing
senses.titleCN: 微小成分：大事物里的一小点
senses.definition: a very small element or ingredient within a larger whole, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 较大整体中极小的成分或要素，用于比喻
senses.example: A molecule of doubt remained in his mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他心里还留着一丝疑虑。
senses.why: The figurative sense treats an idea as a substance with parts. One molecule of doubt is the smallest part that still counts as doubt, exactly as a molecule is the smallest part that still counts as the substance.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义把念头当作有组成部分的物质。一丝疑虑就是还算得上疑虑的最小部分，正如一个分子是还算得上该物质的最小部分。

intro.en: Molecule comes through French molécule from Latin molecula, a diminutive of moles 'mass, heap, massive structure'. The early sense was simply 'a small mass'. Modern chemistry fixed the meaning as a bonded group of atoms in the early 19th century, after Avogadro distinguished molecules from atoms. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: molecule 经法语 molécule 来自拉丁语 molecula，即 moles「块体、堆、庞大结构」的指小形式。早期义只是「一小团物质」。现代化学在 19 世纪初把词义固定为成键的原子团，此前阿伏伽德罗已区分分子与原子。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Chemistry fixes molecule as a bonded group of atoms, and single-molecule work appears much later with sharper instruments.
items.cn: 化学把 molecule 固定为成键的原子团；单分子研究则要晚得多，随着更精细的仪器才出现。

items.en: English molecule is borrowed in the general sense of a small mass or particle, before any chemical definition.
items.cn: 英语 molecule 在尚无化学定义时借入，泛指一小团物质或微粒。

items.en: French molécule is coined from the Latin diminutive as part of early corpuscular theory.
items.cn: 法语 molécule 由拉丁指小形式造出，属于早期微粒说的一部分。

items.en: molecula is moles 'mass' plus the diminutive -cula; it means a small mass, not a bonded group.
items.cn: molecula 是 moles「块体」加指小成分 -cula，意为小团物质，不是成键的原子团。

items.en: The origin of moles beyond Latin is of uncertain origin and is not securely tied to a reconstructed root.
items.cn: moles 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，未能可靠地系于某个重构词根。

note.en: The first group separates three words that look related but are not, or are related only in one sense; the second compares units of matter at different levels.
note.cn: 第一组把三个看似相关、实则无关或只在某一义上相关的词分开；第二组比较不同层级上的物质单元。

entries.definition: a small burrowing animal. This word comes from Germanic roots and has no connection with molecula, despite the identical spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小型穴居动物。这个词出自日耳曼词根，尽管拼写相同，却与 molecula 无关。

entries.definition: a small heap of earth thrown up by a burrowing mole. It belongs with the animal sense, not with the chemical unit.
entries.definitionCN: 鼹鼠刨出的小土堆，属于动物义那一支，与化学单位义无关。

entries.definition: a grinding tooth, from Latin mola 'millstone'. The chemistry adjective molar comes from mole instead, so the two meanings have different histories.
entries.definitionCN: 磨牙，出自拉丁语 mola「磨石」。化学形容词 molar 则出自 mole，两个含义历史不同。

entries.definition: the smallest unit of an element. Atoms are the parts that molecules are built from, so the two words mark different levels.
entries.definitionCN: 元素的最小单元。原子是构成分子的部件，因此两词标记不同层级。

entries.definition: a very small piece of matter. It says nothing about bonds, and may even be larger than a molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质碎块。它不涉及成键，甚至可能比分子还大。

entries.definition: a substance made of two or more elements chemically joined. It names a material, while molecule names one unit of it.
entries.definitionCN: 由两种或以上元素化学结合而成的物质。它命名一种材料，而 molecule 命名该材料的一个单元。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The -cule is a diminutive, so molecule literally begins as 'a small mass'.
normal.cn: -cule 是指小成分，所以 molecule 字面上起于「一小团物质」。

normal.en: Moles also gives demolish, 'to take the mass down', and mole as a breakwater, 'a mass built out'.
normal.cn: moles 还给出 demolish「把块体拆下」以及作防波堤解的 mole「向外筑起的块体」。

normal.en: The chemical unit and the unit of amount are linked: mole is simply molecule shortened.
normal.cn: 化学分子与物质的量单位是相连的：mole 就是 molecule 的缩略。

normal.en: The animal mole shares spelling but not history, so it never appears in chemistry.
normal.cn: 动物义的 mole 只是拼写相同，历史不同，因此从不进入化学语境。

normal.en: A molecule is the smallest piece that still behaves like the substance: split it and the substance is gone.
normal.cn: 分子是仍然表现得像该物质的最小部分：再切开，该物质就不存在了。

abstract.en: See two balls joined by a spring drifting as one body through empty space.
abstract.cn: 想象两个小球被一根弹簧连着，作为一个整体在空处漂移。

abstract.en: Every sense treats the molecule as a smallest whole: smallest unit, smallest particle, smallest trace, smallest ingredient.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都把分子当作一个最小的整体：最小单元、最小颗粒、最少痕迹、最小成分。

abstract.en: The word sits one floor above the atom and one floor below the material.
abstract.cn: 这个词位于原子之上、材料之下的一层。

examples.en: Ozone is a molecule of three oxygen atoms.
examples.cn: 臭氧是由三个氧原子构成的分子。

examples.en: The enzyme breaks each starch molecule into sugars.
examples.cn: 这种酶把每个淀粉分子分解成糖。

examples.en: Not a molecule of the original text survives.
examples.cn: 原文一丝一毫都没有留存下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫利Q」——莫利把Q弹的两个小球连成一小团，飘着走 → molecule 分子

root: 拉丁语 moles「块体、堆」＋指小成分 -cula → molecula「一小团物质」→ 法语 molécule → 英语 molecule。核心是「小到仍是该物质的最小一团」，化学把它定为成键的原子团。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: the smallest group that still counts as the thing. What changes is the frame — a chemical unit, a dust particle, a long biological chain, one observed individual, a free-flying gas unit, a trace, a repeating brick in a polymer, or a small ingredient of an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：仍然算得上「该物」的最小一团。变化的只是框架——化学单元、尘埃颗粒、生物长链、被观测的单个个体、自由飞行的气体单元、一丝痕迹、聚合物中的重复砖块，还是一个念头里的小成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two oxygen atoms held by an invisible bond, drifting as one group.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个氧原子被看不见的键拉着，作为一个整体漂移。

branches.en: THE CHEMICAL UNIT: Latin 'small mass' becomes a bonded group, and long biological chains are still such groups.
branches.cn: 化学单元：拉丁语「小团」变成成键原子团，生物长链也仍是这样的原子团。

branches.en: MERE SIZE: in everyday use any very small particle may be called a molecule, with no chemistry implied.
branches.cn: 仅指大小：日常用法中任何极小的颗粒都可叫 molecule，不含化学意味。

branches.en: ONE UNIT VERSUS MANY: single-molecule work watches one, while kinetic theory treats each as a free traveller.
branches.cn: 一个与许多：单分子研究观察一个，动理论则把每个都当作自由行者。

branches.en: THE TRACE: the smallest imaginable amount borrows the chemist's smallest unit.
branches.cn: 痕迹：想象所及的最少量，借用了化学家的最小单位。

branches.en: THE BRICK AND THE INGREDIENT: polymers repeat one unit, and ideas are said to contain molecules of doubt.
branches.cn: 砖块与成分：聚合物重复同一单元，念头里则被说成含有「一丝」疑虑。

intro.en: Molecule is Latin molecula, a diminutive in -cula built on moles 'mass'. Its English relatives attach the suffixes -ar, -ity and the prefixes macro- and bi-.
intro.cn: molecule 是拉丁语 molecula，由 moles「块体」加指小成分 -cula 构成。它的英语同族词接上 -ar、-ity 后缀以及 macro-、bi- 前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are moles 'mass, heap' and the diminutive -cula. moles also gives demolish and mole in the sense of a breakwater.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 moles「块体、堆」与指小成分 -cula。moles 还给出 demolish 以及作防波堤解的 mole。

items.meaningCN: 保持化学性质的最小单元
items.example: Each molecule of water is bent, not straight.
items.exampleCN: 每个水分子都是弯的，不是直的。

items.example: Molecular bonds store chemical energy.
items.exampleCN: 分子键储存化学能。

items.example: The two forms are molecularly identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两种形式在分子层面完全相同。

items.meaning: the number of molecules taking part in a reaction step
items.meaningCN: 一步反应中参与反应的分子数
items.example: A unimolecular step has molecularity one.
items.exampleCN: 单分子步骤的分子数为一。

items.example: Cellulose is a macromolecule of glucose units.
items.exampleCN: 纤维素是由葡萄糖单元构成的大分子。

items.example: The reaction is bimolecular.
items.exampleCN: 这个反应是双分子的。

items.example: Two moles of gas fill the flask.
items.exampleCN: 两摩尔气体充满这个烧瓶。

items.example: Molar mass is grams per mole.
items.exampleCN: 摩尔质量是每摩尔多少克。

items.example: The crew demolished the chimney.
items.exampleCN: 工人拆掉了烟囱。

items.structure: Latin moles for a great mass
items.meaning: a massive breakwater built into the sea
items.example: Waves break against the mole.
items.exampleCN: 浪拍在防波堤上。

latinEntries.meaning: a mass, a heap, a massive structure

definition_zh: 软体动物（身体柔软、通常带壳的无脊椎动物）
definition_en: a soft-bodied invertebrate, usually protected by a shell, such as a snail, oyster or squid
core_image: 一枚湿亮的螺壳贴在礁石上，壳口探出一小段柔软的身体
scene: 退潮后的礁石上，一只螺用宽大的软足慢慢爬行，背上的螺壳随身体一起移动。 A mollusk crept across the wet rock, its soft foot gripping the surface beneath a spiral shell.
sceneCN: 这里 mollusk 指「软体动物」（第 1 个义项：身体柔软、通常带壳的无脊椎动物）；句意为一枚软体动物靠柔软的足在湿岩上爬行，背上背着螺壳。

pos.zh: 软体动物；贝类

senses.title: A member of the phylum Mollusca
senses.titleCN: 软体动物门的一个成员
senses.definition: any invertebrate of the large phylum Mollusca, with a soft body, a muscular foot and usually a shell
senses.definitionCN: 软体动物门中任何身体柔软、有肌肉质足、通常带壳的无脊椎动物
senses.example: A mollusk crept across the wet rock beneath a spiral shell.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚软体动物背着螺壳在湿岩上爬行。
senses.why: The name comes from Latin for 'soft', because the body is soft even when the shell is hard.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自拉丁语「柔软」，因为即使壳很硬，身体本身仍是软的。

senses.title: A mollusk eaten as food
senses.definition: an edible mollusk such as a mussel, oyster or scallop
senses.definitionCN: 可食用的软体动物，如贻贝、牡蛎或扇贝
senses.example: The market sells mollusks by the basket.
senses.exampleCN: 市场成篮地卖贝类。
senses.why: Fisheries use the biological word for the catch, so mollusk also names a food category.
senses.whyCN: 渔业用这个生物学词来指渔获，因此 mollusk 也成了一个食品类别。

senses.title: The animal that makes a shell
senses.definition: the living animal whose mantle secretes the calcareous shell found on beaches
senses.definitionCN: 由外套膜分泌钙质外壳、其壳常被冲上海滩的活体动物
senses.example: Every shell on the beach was made by a mollusk.
senses.exampleCN: 海滩上的每一枚贝壳都由软体动物造出。
senses.why: Seashells are the most familiar trace of these animals, so the word is often learned through the shell rather than the body.
senses.whyCN: 贝壳是这类动物最熟悉的痕迹，因此人们常先认识壳，再认识动物。

senses.title: A garden or crop pest
senses.definition: a snail or slug that damages plants and is controlled by gardeners
senses.definitionCN: 损害植物、需由园丁防治的螺或蛞蝓
senses.example: Slugs are mollusks that strip young seedlings overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 蛞蝓是软体动物，一夜之间就能把幼苗啃光。
senses.why: The same phylum includes shell-less garden pests, so the word reaches beyond the sea.
senses.whyCN: 同一门类里还有无壳的园圃害虫，因此这个词的适用范围超出了海洋。

senses.title: A fossil used in dating rock
senses.definition: an ancient mollusk preserved in rock, often used as an index fossil for relative dating
senses.definitionCN: 保存在岩石中的古代软体动物，常用作相对定年的标准化石
senses.example: The limestone layer is dated by the mollusks inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 这层石灰岩靠其中的软体动物化石定年。
senses.why: Mollusks evolved quickly and spread widely, which makes their fossils useful clocks.
senses.whyCN: 软体动物演化快、分布广，因此它们的化石成了好用的时钟。

senses.title: An intermediate host for parasites
senses.definition: a snail in whose body a parasitic worm passes one stage of its life cycle
senses.definitionCN: 寄生虫在其体内度过一个生活史阶段的螺
senses.example: The disease spreads through a freshwater mollusk.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病通过一种淡水螺传播。
senses.why: Public health texts name the snail simply as a mollusk when describing the transmission chain.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生文献在描述传播链时，常直接把这个螺称为 mollusk。

senses.title: A laboratory model animal
senses.definition: a mollusk used in research, especially the squid for studies of nerve conduction
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究的软体动物，尤指用于神经传导研究的鱿鱼
senses.example: The squid giant axon made a mollusk central to neuroscience.
senses.exampleCN: 鱿鱼的巨大轴突使一种软体动物成为神经科学的核心。
senses.why: The squid's unusually large nerve fibre made a mollusk the easiest animal in which to measure a nerve impulse.
senses.whyCN: 鱿鱼异常粗大的神经纤维，使一种软体动物成为最容易测量神经冲动的动物。

senses.title: A farmed or invasive species
senses.definition: a mollusk cultivated for food or one that has spread beyond its native range
senses.definitionCN: 为食用而养殖、或已扩散到原分布区之外的软体动物
senses.example: The Pacific oyster is a mollusk farmed on every continent.
senses.exampleCN: 太平洋牡蛎是一种在各大洲都养殖的软体动物。
senses.why: Aquaculture and invasion biology both need a neutral group label, and mollusk supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 水产养殖与入侵生物学都需要一个中性的类群标签，mollusk 正好提供。

intro.en: Mollusk goes back to Latin mollis 'soft' through the adjective molluscus; it is a scientific borrowing that replaced older popular names. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mollusk 经形容词 molluscus 上溯到拉丁 mollis「柔软」；它是科学借词，取代了更早的通俗名称。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mollis meant 'soft, tender, pliant', and molluscus meant 'soft, soft-shelled'. The deeper Indo-European root proposed for mollis is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mollis 意为「柔软的、柔韧的」，molluscus 意为「软的、软壳的」。为 mollis 提出的更早印欧词根属重构形式。

items.en: French naturalists used mollusque for this group in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and English borrowed the term from French.
items.cn: 法国博物学家在 17、18 世纪用 mollusque 指这个类群，英语从法语借入该词。

items.en: Greek natural history had grouped soft-bodied sea animals under a word meaning 'soft things'; Latin mollusca continued that idea rather than inventing it.
items.cn: 希腊自然史早已用意为「柔软之物」的词来归拢身体柔软的海生动物；拉丁 mollusca 延续了这一思路，而非凭空创造。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century zoology fixed Mollusca as a major animal group, and English mollusk followed the scientific Latin.
items.cn: 18、19 世纪动物学把 Mollusca 固定为一个主要动物类群，英语 mollusk 随科学拉丁语而定。

items.en: British usage prefers mollusc, American usage mollusk; both come from the same Latin adjective and neither is more original.
items.cn: 英式用法偏用 mollusc，美式用法偏用 mollusk；两者都出自同一个拉丁形容词，无所谓谁更原始。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): the Latin and French history is clear, but the pre-Latin root of mollis is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：拉丁与法语阶段清楚，但 mollis 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式，并非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one holds spellings and derivatives of the same word, plus one dangerous look-alike; group two holds shelled sea animals that are often confused with mollusks.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的拼写与派生形式，外加一个危险的形近词；第二组是常与软体动物混淆的带壳海生动物。

entries.definition: The same animal under the British spelling; the difference is orthographic, not biological.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个动物的英式拼写；差别在正字法，不在生物学。

entries.definition: The relational adjective 'of mollusks'; it cannot stand for the animal itself.
entries.definitionCN: 表关系的形容词「软体动物的」；它不能代替动物本身。

entries.definition: A substance that kills mollusks, built with -cide 'killing'; it is a chemical, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 杀软体动物的药剂，由 -cide「杀」构成；它是化学品，不是动物。

entries.definition: From Latin mucus 'slime', not mollis 'soft'; the similar sound is accidental, and mucus is a secretion.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 mucus「黏液」，而非 mollis「柔软」；读音相近属偶然，mucus 是分泌物。

entries.definition: A market and fisheries word for edible mollusks and crustaceans together, so it is broader and less precise.
entries.definitionCN: 市场与渔业用语，兼指可食的软体动物与甲壳动物，因此更宽泛、更不精确。

entries.definition: A mollusk with two hinged shells, such as a clam or oyster; it is one class within the mollusks.
entries.definitionCN: 有两片铰合壳的软体动物，如蛤或牡蛎；它是软体动物中的一个纲。

entries.definition: A mollusk that moves on a muscular foot, such as a snail or slug; the name means 'stomach-foot'.
entries.definitionCN: 靠肌肉质足移动的软体动物，如螺或蛞蝓；名字意为「腹足」。

entries.definition: A mollusk with arms around the head, such as a squid or octopus; the name means 'head-foot'.
entries.definitionCN: 头部环生腕足的软体动物，如鱿鱼或章鱼；名字意为「头足」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root moll- means 'soft': a mollusk is the soft-bodied animal, shell or no shell.
normal.cn: 词根 moll- 意为「柔软」：软体动物就是身体柔软，有没有壳都一样。

normal.en: British mollusc and American mollusk are the same word in two spellings.
normal.cn: 英式 mollusc 与美式 mollusk 是同一个词的两种拼写。

normal.en: Bivalve, gastropod and cephalopod are the three mollusk classes most people meet.
normal.cn: 双壳类、腹足类、头足类是普通人最常遇到的三类软体动物。

normal.en: Shellfish is the market word; mollusk is the biological one.
normal.cn: shellfish 是市场用语；mollusk 是生物学用语。

normal.en: Molluscicide kills mollusks the way insecticide kills insects.
normal.cn: molluscicide 杀软体动物，正如 insecticide 杀虫。

abstract.en: Picture a soft body carrying its own house on its back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个柔软的身体把自家的房子背在背上。

abstract.en: Picture a shell on a beach as the only letter left by a writer.
abstract.cn: 想象海滩上一枚贝壳，是作者留下的唯一一封信。

abstract.en: Picture a squid nerve so thick that it made an entire science possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一根粗到足以让一整门科学成为可能的鱿鱼神经。

examples.en: The reef supports mollusks, crustaceans and many kinds of fish.
examples.cn: 这片礁养活软体动物、甲壳动物和许多种鱼。

examples.en: A single mollusk can filter several litres of water a day.
examples.cn: 一只软体动物一天能滤过好几升水。

examples.en: The fossil mollusks show that the basin was once under warm sea.
examples.cn: 软体动物化石表明这个盆地曾位于温暖的海洋之下。

dict_mnemonic.text: mollusk 读起来像「摸了个壳」——伸手一摸，摸到个软乎乎的带壳动物，就是软体动物

root: 拉丁 mollis「柔软」→ molluscus「柔软的、软壳的」→ 法语 mollusque；更早的印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a soft body into different roles: a phylum member, a food, a shell-maker, a garden pest, a fossil clock, a parasite host, a laboratory model and a farmed or invading species.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个柔软的身体进入不同角色：门类成员、食物、造壳者、园圃害虫、化石时钟、寄生虫宿主、实验模式动物，以及养殖或入侵的物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft body under a hard spiral shell, wet rock beneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬螺旋壳下的一团软身体，下面是湿岩。

branches.en: BODY AND HOUSE: the soft animal builds and carries a hard shell.
branches.cn: 身体与房子：柔软的身体造出并背着硬壳。

branches.en: FOOD: fisheries turn the animal into a market category.
branches.cn: 食物：渔业把这种动物变成市场类别。

branches.en: LAND PEST: the same phylum includes slugs in the garden.
branches.cn: 陆上害虫：同一门类也包括园子里的蛞蝓。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: shell chemistry makes the fossil a dating tool.
branches.cn: 深时：壳的化学成分使化石成为定年工具。

branches.en: USES BY OTHERS: a worm's host, a neuroscientist's model, a farmer's stock.
branches.cn: 被他人利用：寄生虫的宿主、神经科学家的模型、养殖者的存栏。

intro.en: Mollusk is a borrowed scientific noun; its English family is built with -an, -cide and compounds rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: mollusk 是借入的科学名词；其英语词族靠 -an、-cide 与复合构成，而非加前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin mollis 'soft' gives molluscus and the scientific group name Mollusca; French mollusque is the direct source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mollis「柔软」衍生 molluscus 与科学类群名 Mollusca；法语 mollusque 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The root explains why a hard shell still hides a soft animal.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根解释了为何硬壳里仍是软身体。

items.example: The ending came into English with the French noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾随法语名词一起进入英语。

items.example: A mollusk crept over the rock.
items.exampleCN: 一只软体动物爬过岩石。

items.example: Mollusks dominate the shell hash on this beach.
items.exampleCN: 这片海滩的贝壳碎屑以软体动物为主。

items.example: The suffix makes the relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表关系的形容词。

items.example: The molluscan shell grew in yearly bands.
items.exampleCN: 软体动物的壳按年轮生长。

items.example: The pond was treated with a molluscicide before the snails were counted.
items.exampleCN: 在统计螺类数量之前，池塘先用了杀软体动物剂。

items.example: British textbooks write mollusc.
items.exampleCN: 英国教材写作 mollusc。

definition_zh: 熔化的；（金属、岩石）熔融的；浇铸成的
definition_en: made liquid by great heat, especially metal or rock; shaped by being poured while melted
core_image: 炉口倾出的铁水在砂模沟槽里铺开，暗红的光顺槽流动，冷却后凝成一块硬物
scene: 铸工打开炉门，橙红色的金属液顺着沟槽流进砂模，空气里全是热浪。The molten iron ran along the channel and filled the sand mould.
sceneCN: 这里 molten 指「经高温熔化后呈液态的」（第 1 个义项：因高热熔成液体，多指金属或岩石）；句意为熔化的铁水沿沟槽流下，灌满砂模。可辨识物件：炉门、铁水沟槽、砂模、热浪。

pos.zh: 熔化的；熔融的；浇铸成的
melt 的过去分词（古旧或方言用法，表示已熔化）

derivatives.zh: 熔化；融化的；令人怜惜的

senses.title: Metal made liquid by heat
senses.definition: of metal: melted and still liquid because of intense heat
senses.definitionCN: 指金属因高温熔化而处于液态
senses.example: The molten iron ran along the channel and filled the sand mould.
senses.exampleCN: 熔化的铁水沿沟槽流下，灌满了砂模。
senses.why: molten is the old past participle of melt, and -en in broken, frozen and spoken marks a finished state, so the word describes metal that has already been liquefied, not metal that is melting now.
senses.whyCN: molten 是 melt 的古老过去分词，而 broken、frozen、spoken 中的 -en 都标记完成状态，因此这个词说的是「已经熔成液体」的金属，而不是「正在熔化」的金属。

senses.title: Rock melted underground
senses.titleCN: 地下的岩石呈熔融状态
senses.definition: of rock: liquefied by the heat of the earth, as in magma below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石因地热而熔化，如地表之下的岩浆
senses.example: Molten rock rises through cracks in the crust and feeds the volcano.
senses.exampleCN: 熔融的岩石沿地壳裂缝上升，为火山提供物质。
senses.why: the geological sense keeps the same picture but moves it underground, where pressure and heat hold rock in a liquid state that would freeze at the surface.
senses.whyCN: 地质义沿用同一幅图景，只是把它移到地下：在高压与高温下，岩石保持液态，一旦到地表就会凝固。

senses.title: Glass or other material in a furnace
senses.titleCN: 玻璃等材料在炉中熔成液态
senses.definition: of glass, wax or similar material: reduced to liquid in a furnace or crucible
senses.definitionCN: 指玻璃、蜡等材料在炉或坩埚中熔成液体
senses.example: Workers poured the molten glass into a long iron trough.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把熔融的玻璃倒进一条长铁槽。
senses.why: the participle was never limited to metals; any solid that heat turns into a pourable liquid can be called molten, and glass-making fixed the word in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词从来不限于金属；任何被高温变成可倾倒液体的固体都可以叫 molten，制玻璃的工艺把这一义项固定下来。

senses.title: Glowing with heat
senses.definition: so hot that the material glows red, orange or white
senses.definitionCN: 指温度高到发出红、橙或白色光
senses.example: The molten core of the furnace lit the whole workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 炉膛里熔融的核心照亮了整个车间。
senses.why: a liquid at such temperatures radiates visible light, so molten naturally extends from 'liquid by heat' to 'glowing because of heat'.
senses.whyCN: 处于这种温度的液体会辐射可见光，因此 molten 从「因热成液」自然延伸到「因热发光」。

senses.title: Cast from melted material
senses.titleCN: 用熔化的材料浇铸成型
senses.definition: formed by pouring melted material into a mould and letting it harden
senses.definitionCN: 指把熔化的材料倒入模具、冷却硬化而成形
senses.example: A molten bronze horse was cast in a single pour.
senses.exampleCN: 一匹熔铜的马在一次浇铸中成型。
senses.why: casting is the practical use of the participle: the material is molten at the moment of the pour, and the shape it takes is the shape of the mould.
senses.whyCN: 浇铸是这个分词的实际用途：材料在倾倒的一刻是熔融的，它得到的形状就是模具的形状。

senses.title: High-temperature liquid in chemistry
senses.titleCN: 化学中的高温熔融体系
senses.definition: of a salt or reagent: melted and used as a liquid medium at high temperature
senses.definitionCN: 指盐或试剂在高温下熔成液体并作为反应介质
senses.example: Molten salt stores heat in the plant's thermal tanks.
senses.exampleCN: 熔盐在电厂的热罐中储存热量。
senses.why: in industrial chemistry the participle becomes a technical label: a molten salt is a liquid ionic medium, not water-based and not a solution.
senses.whyCN: 在工业化学中，这个分词成了技术标签：熔盐是液态离子介质，既不是水溶液，也不是溶剂中的溶液。

senses.title: Flowing light or colour in description
senses.titleCN: 描写中流动的光或色彩
senses.definition: literary: of light or colour, glowing and fluid as if poured
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法：指光或色彩如被倾倒般流动、灼亮
senses.example: The molten gold of sunset spilled across the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 落日熔金般的光铺满海湾。
senses.why: the image of poured metal gives writers a way to describe light that seems liquid, and this figurative use keeps the heat and the flow of the original picture.
senses.whyCN: 「倾倒金属」的形象给写作者提供了描写看似液态的光的办法，这一比喻义保留了原图景中的高温与流动。

senses.title: Intense, barely contained feeling
senses.titleCN: 强烈而几乎压不住的情绪
senses.definition: figurative: of anger, energy or passion, so intense that it seems to burn and flow
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：指愤怒、能量或激情强烈到仿佛在燃烧、流动
senses.example: Her molten anger frightened everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她如熔岩般的怒火让屋里所有人都害怕。
senses.why: heat and loss of shape are the two parts of the image, and both transfer to emotion: something solid has become dangerous, moving and hot.
senses.whyCN: 高温与失去形状是这幅图景的两个部分，两者都能转移到情绪上：原本稳固的东西变得危险、流动而灼热。

intro.en: Molten is the old past participle of the English verb melt, and its history is the history of that verb rather than of a Latin borrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: molten 是英语动词 melt 的古老过去分词，它的历史就是 melt 这个词的历史，而不是一次拉丁语借词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Meltan meant 'to melt, become liquid, dissolve' and also 'to digest' in the bodily sense; the verb is recorded in Old English before the Norman period.
items.cn: meltan 意为「熔化、变成液体、溶解」，也指身体意义上的「消化」；这个词在诺曼征服之前的古英语中已有记录。

items.en: *Meltanan is a reconstruction supported by Old Norse melta and Old High German smelzan 'to melt'; no single attested form of the root survives outside the Germanic group.
items.cn: *meltanan 是重构形式，依据古诺斯语 melta 与古高地德语 smelzan「熔化」；这个词根在日耳曼语族之外没有留存下来的单一形式。

items.en: The ending -en marks a completed state in strong past participles such as broken, frozen, spoken and molten, so the form says 'already melted' rather than 'melting'.
items.cn: 后缀 -en 在 broken、frozen、spoken、molten 这类强变化过去分词中标记完成状态，因此这一形式说的是「已经熔化」，而不是「正在熔化」。

items.en: In Middle English molten is recorded of liquefied metal, wax and ore, usually in the phrase 'molten lead' or 'molten metal'.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，molten 已用于熔化的金属、蜡与矿石，常见于「熔铅」「熔融金属」这类说法。

items.en: From the seventeenth century metallurgy fixed the word in phrases such as molten iron, and geology later applied it to magma and lava; the technical senses keep the participle's perfect meaning.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，冶金学用 molten iron（铁水）这类说法把词固定下来，地质学后来把它用于岩浆与熔岩；这些技术义都保留了分词的完成意味。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic history of *meltanan is unsettled, and the old comparison with Latin mollis 'soft' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation; any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：*meltanan 在日耳曼语之前的历史没有定论，把它与拉丁 mollis「软」相比只是假说，并非已证实的派生；凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one collects words that look or sound like molten but come from other roots; group two collects words for the same physical state of matter.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音近似但词根不同的词；第二组是描述同一物态的词。

entries.definition: Means to shed feathers, hair or skin, and comes from a separate Germanic and Old French line; the resemblance to molten is only in sound and spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 意为脱换羽毛、毛发或外皮，来自另一条日耳曼语与古法语线索；与 molten 的相似只在音形。

entries.definition: To extract metal from ore by heating, from Middle Dutch smelten 'to melt'; it is a Germanic relative of melt rather than a form of molten itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指加热矿石以提炼金属，来自中古荷兰语 smelten「熔化」；它是 melt 在日耳曼语中的亲属，而不是 molten 本身的一个形式。

entries.definition: A hollow form for casting, or the verb to shape something; it goes back through Old French to Latin modulus 'small measure', so it is not related to melt at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指浇铸用的凹型，或「塑造」这一动词；它经古法语上溯到拉丁 modulus「小量度」，与 melt 毫无词源关系。

entries.definition: The regular past participle of melt, used for anything that has melted, from butter to snow; molten is the older form and today mostly describes metal, rock and glass.
entries.definitionCN: melt 的规则过去分词，可用于黄油、积雪等任何融化之物；molten 是较早的形式，今天多用于金属、岩石与玻璃。

entries.definition: A formal or technical word for turning a solid into a liquid, from Latin liquere 'be fluid'; it states the result without the image of a furnace.
entries.definitionCN: 使固体变成液体的正式或技术用词，来自拉丁 liquere「呈液态」；它只陈述结果，不带炉火的形象。

entries.definition: Describes an object glowing with heat, from Latin candere 'to shine'; it names the light rather than the liquid state that molten includes.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体因高温而发光，来自拉丁 candere「发光」；它命名的是光，而 molten 还包含液态这一层。

entries.definition: Means melted together into one mass, from Latin fundere 'to pour'; it stresses union, where molten stresses the liquid condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指经热熔合为一体，来自拉丁 fundere「倾倒」；它强调结合，molten 强调液态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real participle ending, the real word family and the fixed technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的分词后缀、真实的词族与固定技术搭配。

normal.en: Melt plus -en: the same ending as in broken, frozen and spoken, all marking a finished state.
normal.cn: melt 加 -en：与 broken、frozen、spoken 同一个后缀，都标记完成状态。

normal.en: The family runs melt, melting, melted, meltwater, meltdown, remelt.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 melt、melting、melted、meltwater、meltdown、remelt。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the sense: molten metal, molten rock, molten glass, molten salt.
normal.cn: 固定搭配承载词义：熔融金属、熔融岩石、熔融玻璃、熔盐。

normal.en: In geology the word pairs with magma below ground and lava above ground.
normal.cn: 在地质学中，这个词与地下的岩浆、地表的熔岩配对使用。

normal.en: Metallurgy supplies the everyday picture: molten iron is poured, never hammered.
normal.cn: 冶金学提供日常图景：铁水只能浇，不能锤。

abstract.en: Picture a candle that has lost its shape but kept all its wax.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛失去了形状，却保留了全部的蜡。

abstract.en: Picture a winter stream freezing into one flat sheet of glass.
abstract.cn: 想象冬天的小溪冻成一整片平玻璃。

abstract.en: Picture an argument heated until it becomes one glowing thread.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争论被加热到只剩一根发亮的线。

examples.en: The foundry pours molten steel into ingots every four hours.
examples.cn: 铸造厂每隔四小时把钢水浇进钢锭模。

examples.en: Molten rock beneath the ridge pushes the crust upward.
examples.cn: 山脊之下的熔融岩石把地壳向上顶。

examples.en: The glassblower shaped the molten glass with a long iron pipe.
examples.cn: 吹玻璃工用长铁管给熔融玻璃塑形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩（mō）+ 尔（l）+ 腾（tén）」——热到腾起来、化成液体 → 熔化的

root: 古英语 meltan「熔化」的过去分词，属日耳曼语 *meltanan（重构形式）；后缀 -en 标记完成状态。更深来源不确定，与拉丁 mollis「软」的比较仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one physical event: solid material is heated until it can flow, and then that same event is used for glowing light, for casting, for industrial chemistry and finally for emotion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个物理事件展开：固体被加热到可以流动，这个事件随后被用于发光、浇铸、工业化学，最后用于情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a furnace mouth where solid metal leaves its shape and becomes a glowing stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：炉口处，固态金属失去形状，变成一道发光的流体。

branches.en: MATERIALS THAT MELT: iron in a ladle and rock under a volcano obey the same rule.
branches.cn: 会熔的材料：勺里的铁与火山下的岩石遵守同一条规则。

branches.en: FURNACE AND PLANT: glass in a crucible and salt in a thermal tank are both molten media.
branches.cn: 炉与厂：坩埚里的玻璃与热罐里的盐都是熔融介质。

branches.en: GLOW: heat so great that the liquid itself becomes the light source.
branches.cn: 发光：热到液体本身成为光源。

branches.en: CASTING: the liquid is given a shape during the moment it can flow.
branches.cn: 浇铸：在能够流动的那一刻，液体被赋予形状。

branches.en: IMAGE TRANSFER: poured light and molten anger keep the same heat and flow.
branches.cn: 意象转移：倾倒的光与熔岩般的怒火保留了同样的热与流动。

intro.en: Molten is an English participle rather than a Latin compound, but its ending and its family are still readable morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: molten 是英语分词而非拉丁复合词，但它的后缀与词族仍可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: No Latin relative is reliable here: the verb is Germanic, and Latin mollis 'soft' is only a hypothesis, so the Latin entries are left empty rather than invented.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有可靠的拉丁同族词：该动词属日耳曼语，拉丁 mollis「软」只是假说，因此拉丁条目留空，不作编造。

items.example: The snow melted before noon.
items.exampleCN: 雪在中午前融化了。

items.example: Broken glass lay on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 碎玻璃摊在地上。

items.example: The molten iron ran along the channel.
items.exampleCN: 铁水沿沟槽流下。

items.meaning: in the process of becoming liquid
items.example: The melting ice fed the stream.
items.exampleCN: 融冰补给着溪流。

items.example: Melted wax sealed the letter.
items.exampleCN: 熔蜡封住了信口。

items.meaning: water released by melting ice or snow
items.meaningCN: 冰川或积雪融化产生的水
items.example: Meltwater cut a narrow channel.
items.exampleCN: 融水切出一条窄沟。

items.meaning: a reactor accident, or a total collapse
items.example: The meltdown ruined the reactor core.
items.exampleCN: 熔毁损毁了反应堆堆芯。

items.example: The coating is meltable at low heat.
items.exampleCN: 这层涂料低温即可熔化。

items.meaning: to melt something a second time
items.example: Scrap steel is remelted in an electric furnace.
items.exampleCN: 废钢在电炉中再熔。

definition_zh: 动量；冲力；势头；推动力；干劲
definition_en: the force that keeps a moving body going, or the growing drive behind a process
core_image: 一块石球顺着斜坡滚下，越滚越快，身后的尘土被推开成一条直线
scene: 接力赛最后一棒交到手上时，队伍已经领先半步，看台上的人开始提前欢呼。The runner carried the team's momentum through the final bend.
sceneCN: 这里 momentum 指已经积起、还会继续往前推的势头（第 3 个义项：进程累积起来的推进势头）；句意为跑者带着队伍已有的势头跑过最后一个弯道。图中可辨识物件：接力棒、弯道标记线、看台栏杆、扬起的尘土。

pos.zh: 动量；冲力；势头；推动力；干劲

derivatives.zh: 重大的；影响深远的（同一拉丁词干加形容词后缀）
片刻的；短暂的（同一词干加表示持续的后缀）

senses.title: Quantity of motion in physics
senses.titleCN: 物理学中质量与速度相乘的动量
senses.definition: a physical quantity equal to the mass of a moving body multiplied by its velocity
senses.definitionCN: 运动物体的质量与其速度相乘所得的物理量
senses.example: The cart's momentum doubled when its speed doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 小车的速度翻倍时，它的动量也翻倍。
senses.why: Seventeenth-century mechanics needed a name for the amount of motion a body carries, and took the Latin word for movement itself.
senses.whyCN: 十七世纪的力学需要给物体携带的「运动量」一个名字，于是直接取用了拉丁语中表示「运动」的那个词。

senses.title: The carrying force of a moving body
senses.titleCN: 运动物体带着向前冲的力量
senses.definition: the push that a moving body carries and that keeps it going until something stops it
senses.definitionCN: 运动物体所携带、并使其在受阻前持续前进的推力
senses.example: The loaded truck's momentum carried it through the intersection.
senses.exampleCN: 满载卡车的冲力使它冲过了十字路口。
senses.why: Once the word named a quantity, speakers used it for the felt push of a heavy body that will not stop at once.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词被用来指一个量之后，人们又用它来指重物那种不能立刻停下的可感推力。

senses.title: A process gaining strength
senses.titleCN: 事情逐渐积累起来的推进势头
senses.definition: the increasing strength of a process or movement that makes it hard to stop
senses.definitionCN: 某项进程或运动不断增强、难以遏止的力量
senses.example: The campaign gained momentum after the first debate.
senses.exampleCN: 首场辩论之后，这场竞选势头渐起。
senses.why: A process that keeps advancing looks like a body that keeps rolling, so the physical word was carried over to social change.
senses.whyCN: 不断推进的进程看起来就像持续滚动的物体，于是这个物理词被移用到社会变化上。

senses.title: A driving force behind change
senses.titleCN: 推动变化发生的外部动力
senses.definition: a force or factor that drives change forward in a field or economy
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域或经济中把变化向前推动的力量或因素
senses.example: Cheap rail gave the inland trade fresh momentum.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的铁路给内陆贸易带来了新的动力。
senses.why: Here the word shifts from the thing moving to the force that sets it moving, a common reversal of cause and effect.
senses.whyCN: 这里词义从「在动的东西」转到「使它动起来的力量」，是因果位置常见的互换。

senses.title: Personal drive or energy
senses.definition: the energy and confidence that keep a person working toward a goal
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人持续朝目标努力的精力与信心
senses.example: She lost momentum after the first rejection letter.
senses.exampleCN: 收到第一封拒信后，她就泄了劲。
senses.why: The image of a rolling body was applied to a person's inner motion, so that drive could be gained or lost like speed.
senses.whyCN: 滚动物体的画面被用到人内心的运动上，于是干劲也像速度一样可以增减。

senses.title: The upper hand in a contest
senses.titleCN: 比赛中占据上风的势头
senses.definition: the advantage a team or player holds when events start to favour them
senses.definitionCN: 当局势开始偏向一方时，该队或该选手所占的优势
senses.example: The home team seized momentum in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在下半场掌握了势头。
senses.why: In sport the physical sense narrows to the side that is rolling forward while the other is trying to stop it.
senses.whyCN: 在体育中，这个物理义收窄为：一方正向前滚动，另一方则试图把它拦住。

senses.title: Directional strength in markets
senses.titleCN: 市场中价格延续原方向的动能
senses.definition: the tendency of a price or market to keep moving in the same direction
senses.definitionCN: 价格或市场倾向于沿同一方向继续运动的力量
senses.example: Traders watch for momentum before buying a currency.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员在买入某种货币之前会先看它的动能。
senses.why: Technical analysis borrowed the physics term because a rising price was treated as a body with inertia of its own.
senses.whyCN: 技术分析借用了这个物理词，因为上涨的价格被当作一个自带惯性的物体。

senses.title: The unstoppable course of history
senses.titleCN: 历史或改革难以阻挡的进程
senses.definition: the collective force that keeps a large historical change moving forward
senses.definitionCN: 使大规模历史变化持续前进的集体力量
senses.example: The momentum of reform survived two changes of cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 改革的势头挺过了两次内阁更替。
senses.why: The largest rolling body speakers can imagine is history itself, so the word ends by naming a collective movement.
senses.whyCN: 人们能想象的最大滚动物体就是历史本身，于是这个词最终用来指一种集体运动。

intro.en: Momentum comes from Latin momentum 'movement, moving power', built on the stem of movere 'to move' with the noun suffix -mentum; the physics sense was fixed after the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: momentum 来自拉丁 momentum「运动、推动力」，由 movere「移动」的词干加名词后缀 -mentum 构成；物理的「动量」义在十七世纪以后固定下来。

items.en: Movere meant to move or set something in motion, and its stem mov- supplied the verb behind the noun.
items.cn: movere 意为「移动、使某物动起来」，它的词干提供了这个名词背后的动词。

items.en: Momentum named a movement, the power that produces movement, and also a brief moment of time.
items.cn: momentum 指一次运动、产生运动的力量，也指短暂的一瞬。

items.en: The suffix -mentum turned a verb stem into a noun of action or result, the same ending seen in monumentum.
items.cn: 后缀 -mentum 把动词词干变成表示动作或结果的名词，与 monumentum 用的是同一个词尾。

items.en: Mechanics adopted the word for the measured quantity of motion, mass times velocity, and that reading became standard.
items.cn: 力学采用这个词来指可测量的运动量，即质量乘速度，这一读法后来成为标准。

items.en: From the rolling body the word spread to campaigns, markets and personal energy, all of which can gain or lose speed.
items.cn: 从滚动物体出发，这个词扩展到竞选、市场与个人精力，这些事物都能加速或减速。

items.en: The earliest recorded dates for the separate senses are approximate; the Latin noun itself is well attested.
items.cn: 各义项的最早记录年代为约数；这个拉丁名词本身已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like momentum; the second group names neighbouring kinds of force and speed.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 momentum 相近；第二组是意思相邻的其他「力、速度」说法。

entries.definition: A point in time; it is a shortened form of the same Latin noun that gave momentum, not a derivative built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一时刻；它是同一个拉丁名词经法语缩略而来，并不是由 momentum 加缀派生。

entries.definition: Weighty or important; built on moment with an adjective suffix, it has nothing to do with physical motion.
entries.definitionCN: 意为重大、要紧；由 moment 加形容词后缀构成，与物理运动无关。

entries.definition: Lasting only a moment; the suffix marks duration, not the carrying of motion.
entries.definitionCN: 意为只持续一瞬；后缀标的是时长，而不是携带的运动。

entries.definition: The general noun for moving or a concerted campaign; it lacks the idea of a measured quantity carried forward.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指移动或一场有组织的运动；它没有「被携带的可测量之量」这层意思。

entries.definition: A keepsake or reminder; it comes from Latin memento 'remember', a different root, and only looks like momentum.
entries.definitionCN: 指纪念品或提醒物；来自拉丁 memento「记住」，词根不同，只是形近。

entries.definition: A force that starts something moving; from Latin impetere 'to attack', a different root from movere.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物开始运动的力量；来自拉丁 impetere「攻击」，与 movere 不同源。

entries.definition: Speed in a stated direction; it measures how fast, while momentum also takes mass into account.
entries.definitionCN: 沿指定方向的速度；它只衡量快慢，而 momentum 还把质量算进去。

entries.definition: The forward push of an engine or a hand; it names the push itself rather than the quantity a body carries.
entries.definitionCN: 发动机或手向前的推力；它指推力本身，而非物体携带的量。

entries.definition: Inner energy or an organized effort; it sits closer to the personal sense than to the physical one.
entries.definitionCN: 内心的干劲或一场有组织的努力；比物理义更贴近个人层面。

entries.definition: A sudden push, or in physics the change of momentum; from Latin pellere, a root different from movere.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的一推，物理学中也指动量的变化；来自拉丁 pellere，与 movere 不同源。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for to move, so momentum is the movement itself turned into a noun.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，momentum 就是把「运动」本身变成名词。

normal.en: The family runs moment, momentary, momentous and movement, all from the same Latin stem.
normal.cn: 同族词有 moment、momentary、momentous 与 movement，都出自同一拉丁词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: gain momentum, lose momentum, gather momentum.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：获得势头、失去势头、积聚势头。

normal.en: The noun suffix -mentum is the same one heard in monumentum, a thing that brings something to mind.
normal.cn: 名词后缀 -mentum 与 monumentum 相同，后者指让人想起某事的事物。

normal.en: In school physics the quantity is written as mass times velocity, which is exactly momentum.
normal.cn: 学校物理里把这个量写成质量乘速度，那正是动量。

abstract.en: Picture a stone rolling down a slope, and the dust behind it standing in a straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头顺坡滚下，身后尘土立成一条直线。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd already walking in one direction; nobody has to push it, it simply keeps going.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人已经朝同一个方向走，没人推，他们只是继续走。

abstract.en: Picture a flywheel so heavy that the whole workshop slows when someone switches it off.
abstract.cn: 想象一只极重的飞轮，有人关掉它时整间工坊都跟着慢下来。

examples.en: The flywheel stores momentum and smooths the engine's pulses.
examples.cn: 飞轮储存动量，使发动机的脉动变得平顺。

examples.en: The study measured how much momentum the debris carried after the impact.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了碎片在撞击后携带了多少动量。

examples.en: Public support for the ban gained momentum after the drought.
examples.cn: 干旱之后，公众对这项禁令的支持势头渐起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸门特姆」——摸到了门路，劲头就一路往前推

root: 拉丁 movere「移动」→ 词干 mov- 加名词后缀 -mentum → 拉丁 momentum「运动、推动力」→ 英语 momentum；物理「动量」义在十七世纪以后固定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses track one rolling body: a measured quantity, its carried push, a process speeding up, the force behind it, a person's inner drive, a team's upper hand, a market's direction, and history itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个滚动物体：可测量的量、它携带的推力、逐渐加速的进程、背后的推动力、个人的干劲、一队的上风、市场的方向，最后是历史本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy stone rolls downhill, faster and faster, pushing the dust aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块沉重的石球顺坡滚下，越来越快，把尘土推向两边。

branches.en: THE MEASUREMENT: mass times velocity turns the picture of rolling into a number physics can use.
branches.cn: 可测量：质量乘速度把滚动的画面变成一个物理学能用的数字。

branches.en: THE PUSH FELT: the same body keeps going and shoves aside whatever stands in its way.
branches.cn: 可感的推力：同一个物体继续前进，把挡路的东西推到一边。

branches.en: A PROCESS OR A TEAM THAT IS ROLLING: social campaigns and sports sides both gain speed.
branches.cn: 滚动中的进程或队伍：社会运动与球队都会积累速度。

branches.en: WHAT SETS THINGS ROLLING: the word moves from the moving body to the force behind it, up to history.
branches.cn: 使事物滚动的东西：词义从滚动的物体转到它背后的力量，再扩大到历史。

branches.en: INNER AND MARKET MOTION: a person's drive and a price's direction are private versions of the same roll.
branches.cn: 内心与市场的运动：个人的干劲与价格的方向，是同一滚动的两种私密版本。

intro.en: Momentum is built from the Latin verb movere and the noun suffix -mentum, and the same verb supports several English words.
intro.cn: momentum 由拉丁动词 movere 与名词后缀 -mentum 构成，这个动词还支撑起若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives movement, moment, momentum and motive; the suffix -mentum is the same ending found in monumentum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 movement（移动）、moment（时刻）、momentum（动量）与 motive（动机）；后缀 -mentum 与 monumentum 用的是同一个词尾。

items.meaning: to move; to set in motion
items.example: The verb supplies the whole image of something set rolling.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了「使某物滚动起来」的完整画面。

items.structure: stem of movere used before suffixes
items.example: The bare stem is what the noun suffix attaches to.
items.exampleCN: 名词后缀正是接在这个光秃的词干上。

items.example: It turns a verb of moving into a noun for the movement.
items.exampleCN: 它把表示移动的动词变成指该运动的名词。

items.example: The noun carries both the motion and the force behind it.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时带着运动与推动它的力。

items.structure: shortened from the same Latin noun through French
items.example: The old noun also meant a brief instant, which survives in moment.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老名词也指短暂的一瞬，这一义留在 moment 里。

items.meaning: the act of moving; a campaign
items.example: The English suffix repeats the function of the Latin one.
items.exampleCN: 英语后缀重复了那个拉丁后缀的功能。

items.example: The adjective speaks of consequence, not of speed.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词说的是分量，而不是速度。

items.example: The suffix limits the noun to a very short stretch of time.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把这个名词限定在极短的一段时间里。

items.example: The abstract noun names how short the moment is.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词指那一瞬有多短。

items.example: It only looks like our word and belongs to the memory family.
items.exampleCN: 它只是形近，实际属于「记忆」那一族。

definition_zh: 君主；国王或女王；世袭的国家元首；帝王蛱蝶；某个领域里的霸主；某一方天地中最宏大者
definition_en: a sole hereditary ruler such as a king or queen; also a large migratory butterfly and, figuratively, a dominant person or thing
core_image: 一顶王冠落在唯一的座位上，两侧的座椅都空着
scene: 礼仪厅里只有一张高背椅，椅背刻着王冠，两侧的座位都空着。The monarch opened the session with a short address from the throne.
sceneCN: 这里 monarch 指「唯一的世袭君主」（第 1 个义项：由一人继承国家元首之位）；句意为君主在御座上为会议作简短开幕致辞。可辨识物件：高背椅、王冠、空座位、御座、礼袍。

pos.zh: 君主；国王；女王；帝王蛱蝶；霸主

derivatives.zh: monarch + -y（经拉丁 -ia、希腊 -ia 的状态后缀）→ 君主制，语义由人转为制度
monarch + -ic（希腊 -ikos、拉丁 -icus 形容词后缀）→ 君主的、君主制的
monarch + -ical（形容词后缀变体）→ 君主制的，与 monarchic 近义
monarch + -ism（主义后缀）→ 君主主义，主张保留君主制
monarch + -ist（主张者后缀）→ 君主主义者；拥护君主制的
monarch + -ess（阴性后缀）→ 女君主（较少用）

senses.title: A sole hereditary ruler
senses.definition: a king, queen or emperor who holds office by inheritance and stands alone at the head of the state
senses.definitionCN: 凭继承取得职位、独自居于国家顶端的国王、女王或皇帝
senses.example: The monarch opened the session with a short address from the throne.
senses.exampleCN: 君主在御座上为会议作了简短开幕致辞。
senses.why: Greek monarkhes joined monos 'alone' to arkhein 'rule', so the word begins with the idea of one person ruling.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 monarkhes 把 monos「单独」与 arkhein「统治」结合，词的核心从一开始就是「一人统治」。

senses.title: A constitutional king or queen
senses.titleCN: 立宪制下的国王或女王
senses.definition: a hereditary head of state whose powers are limited by a constitution and exercised through ministers
senses.definitionCN: 世袭的国家元首，其权力受宪法限制、由大臣行使
senses.example: In a constitutional system the monarch reigns but does not rule.
senses.exampleCN: 在立宪制度下，君主在位而不亲政。
senses.why: The title survived even when real power moved to parliament, so monarch now often means a ceremonial sovereign.
senses.whyCN: 即使实权移入议会，称号仍保留，因此 monarch 如今常指礼仪性的元首。

senses.title: An absolute ruler
senses.definition: a ruler who makes law and raises revenue without a representative body
senses.definitionCN: 不经代议机构便立法与征税的统治者
senses.example: The monarch could raise taxes without consulting a council.
senses.exampleCN: 这位君主无需咨询议事会便可加税。
senses.why: The original sense had no constitutional limit, and that older reading survives when historians discuss absolute rule.
senses.whyCN: 原义并无宪法限制，史家讨论专制统治时保留的正是这一较早读法。

senses.title: A migratory orange butterfly
senses.titleCN: 橙色的迁徙性帝王蛱蝶
senses.definition: a large orange-and-black butterfly, Danaus plexippus, famous for its long annual migration
senses.definitionCN: 橙黑相间的大型蛱蝶，以每年长距离迁徙著称
senses.example: A monarch drifted south along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 一只帝王蛱蝶沿着海岸向南飘飞。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century naturalists called the most impressive local butterfly a monarch, borrowing the title of the grandest ruler.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪博物学者把当地最引人注目的蛱蝶称作君主，借用了最高统治者的称号。

senses.title: A dominant figure in a field
senses.definition: a person who dominates an activity or industry as though by royal authority
senses.definitionCN: 像凭王权般支配某项活动或行业的人
senses.example: She was the monarch of the city's concert halls.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这座城市音乐厅的霸主。
senses.why: The metaphor moves sole rule from a state to a social sphere, where one person sets the tone for everyone.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把「一人统治」从国家移到社会领域，一个人便为所有人定调。

senses.title: The ruler of a small state
senses.definition: a ruler of a small kingdom or princely state, especially in historical accounts
senses.definitionCN: 小王国或土邦的统治者，尤见于历史记述
senses.example: The monarch of the island state kept his own coinage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛国的君主保有自己的铸币权。
senses.why: Scale does not change the title: a ruler who holds sole hereditary power is a monarch whatever the size of the map.
senses.whyCN: 规模不改变称号：只要独自掌握世袭权力，无论地图多小都是君主。

senses.title: A magnate compared to a king
senses.definition: a wealthy or powerful magnate described as ruling an industry like a king
senses.definitionCN: 被形容为像国王一样统治某个行业的富有或有权势者
senses.example: The railway monarch travelled in a private carriage.
senses.exampleCN: 这位铁路巨头乘坐私人车厢出行。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century newspapers nicknamed industry barons 'monarchs' because their decisions moved whole regions.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪报纸把产业大亨戏称为「君主」，因为他们的决定能牵动整片地区。

senses.title: The grandest thing of its kind
senses.definition: the largest or most impressive example of a natural kind, imagined as ruling over the rest
senses.definitionCN: 某一自然类别中最大或最壮观的个体，被想象为统辖其余
senses.example: The old oak was called the monarch of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 那棵老橡树被称为林中之王。
senses.why: The same habit that names the biggest butterfly also crowns the biggest tree, so monarch can mean simply the grandest member.
senses.whyCN: 给最大蛱蝶命名的习惯也把最大的树加冕，因此 monarch 可仅指最宏大的那一个。

intro.en: Monarch comes through Latin and French from Greek monarkhes 'sole ruler', built on monos 'alone' and arkhein 'to rule'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monarch 经拉丁与法语来自希腊 monarkhes「唯一统治者」，由 monos「单独」与 arkhein「统治」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Monos meant 'alone, single'; it is the same element found in monologue and monopoly.
items.cn: monos 意为「单独、唯一」，与 monologue、monopoly 中的成分相同。

items.en: Arkhein meant 'to begin, to rule'; its noun arkhe could mean both a starting point and an office of rule.
items.cn: arkhein 意为「开始、统治」；其名词 arkhe 既可指起点，也可指统治职位。

items.en: Monos plus arkhein produced monarkhes, 'one who rules alone', the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: monos 加 arkhein 构成 monarkhes「独自统治的人」，是英语该词的直接来源。

items.en: Latin monarcha kept the Greek meaning and passed it to French monarque and then to English.
items.cn: 拉丁 monarcha 保留了希腊含义，传给法语 monarque，再进入英语。

items.en: The butterfly name is a nineteenth-century naturalist borrowing, and the magnate and 'grandest tree' uses are journalistic extensions of the same image.
items.cn: 蝴蝶名是十九世纪博物学者的借用，巨头义与「林中最高大的树」义都是同一意象的报刊引申。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of monarch for the butterfly is not established, and the naming motive, whether royal colour or size, is a matter of conjecture.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：monarch 用于该蛱蝶的最早记录未有定论，命名动机是王室色彩还是体型，也属推测。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Greek pair or accidental neighbours; group two holds words for a sole ruler.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊组合或偶然相邻的形式；第二组是表示唯一统治者的词。

entries.definition: The system or state of rule by one monarch, from Greek monarkhia; monarch is the person.
entries.definitionCN: 由一位君主统治的制度或国家，出自希腊 monarkhia；monarch 指人。

entries.definition: The relational adjective 'of a monarch or monarchy'.
entries.definitionCN: 「君主的、君主制的」关系形容词。

entries.definition: From Greek monazein 'to live alone', but with no arkhein element: a community of monks, not a ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 monazein「独居」，但无 arkhein 成分：是僧侣团体，不是统治者。

entries.definition: From hieros 'sacred' plus arkhein: rule by priests, later any ranked order. It shares the second element only.
entries.definitionCN: 由 hieros「神圣」加 arkhein 构成：最初指祭司统治，后指任何等级秩序。只共享第二个成分。

entries.definition: The male ruler of a kingdom; a specific rank, while monarch is the general category.
entries.definitionCN: 王国的男性统治者；是具体等级，而 monarch 是总类。

entries.definition: A ruler or state with supreme legal power; it stresses authority rather than heredity.
entries.definitionCN: 握有最高法律权力的统治者或国家；强调权威而非世袭。

entries.definition: The ruler of an empire, traditionally ranked above a king; an emperor is a kind of monarch.
entries.definitionCN: 帝国的统治者，传统等级高于国王；皇帝是君主的一种。

entries.definition: Anyone who governs, elected or not; the neutral word that need not imply a crown.
entries.definitionCN: 任何治理者，无论是否经选举；是不必含王冠的中性词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monos 'alone' + arkhein 'rule': one person rules.
normal.cn: monos「单独」+ arkhein「统治」：一个人统治。

normal.en: The family runs monarch, monarchy, monarchic, monarchical, monarchist, monarchism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monarch、monarchy、monarchic、monarchical、monarchist、monarchism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: constitutional monarch, absolute monarch, reigning monarch.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：立宪君主、专制君主、在位君主。

normal.en: The butterfly keeps the grand title, and so does the biggest tree in the wood.
normal.cn: 蝴蝶保留了这个宏大称号，林中最大的树也一样。

normal.en: monastery also starts with monos but has no arkhein, so it is not a relative.
normal.cn: monastery 也以 monos 开头，却没有 arkhein，因此并非同族词。

abstract.en: Picture one chair in a hall full of empty chairs.
abstract.cn: 想象一间满是空椅的大厅里只坐着一张椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a butterfly carrying a tiny crown across a whole continent.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蝴蝶戴着小小的王冠飞越整块大陆。

abstract.en: Picture an old tree that the village treats as its ruler.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵老树，被全村当作君主。

examples.en: The monarch and the parliament disagreed over the new tax.
examples.cn: 君主与议会就新税发生分歧。

examples.en: Monarchs migrate thousands of kilometres every autumn.
examples.cn: 帝王蛱蝶每年秋天迁徙数千公里。

examples.en: In the trade, he was treated as a monarch whose word settled prices.
examples.cn: 在这一行里，他被当作一句话就能定下价格的君主。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mono」单一 + 「arch」统治——一个人统治全场 → 君主

root: 希腊 monarkhes「唯一统治者」= monos「单独」+ arkhein「统治」；经拉丁 monarcha、法语 monarque 入英语。英语 monarch。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one seat: a single ruler, whether crowned by a constitution, by absolute power, by a magnate's fortune, or only by being the grandest thing in the wood.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都落在同一个座位上：唯一的统治者，无论是宪法所加冕、绝对权力所加冕、巨富所加冕，还是只因为它是林中最大者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one throne in a hall of empty chairs.
core.cn: 核心意象：满是空椅的大厅里只有一张御座。

branches.en: THE SEAT: one person holds the office by inheritance.
branches.cn: 座位：一人凭继承占据职位。

branches.en: TWO LIMITS: the same title covers a ceremonial sovereign and an unlimited autocrat.
branches.cn: 两种界限：同一称号既指礼仪元首，也指不受限的专制者。

branches.en: SMALL MAP: size does not change the title of a sole hereditary ruler.
branches.cn: 小地图：领土大小不改变唯一世袭统治者的称号。

branches.en: BORROWED GRANDEUR: a magnate, a butterfly or a great tree is crowned by metaphor.
branches.cn: 借来的宏大：巨头、蝴蝶或大树都被比喻加冕。

branches.en: THE CREATURE: the most striking local butterfly takes the grandest name.
branches.cn: 生物：当地最引人注目的蛱蝶取用了最宏大的名字。

intro.en: Monarch is a two-morpheme Greek compound, and both halves recur in English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: monarch 是双语素的希腊复合词，两半都在英语词中反复出现，因此整个词族可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek monos and arkhein give monarch, monarchy and monarchic; Latin monarcha and monarchia carried the forms westward.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 monos 与 arkhein 衍生 monarch、monarchy 与 monarchic；拉丁 monarcha 与 monarchia 把这些形式向西传。

items.example: The element also appears in monologue.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 monologue 中。

items.example: The root joins ruling to the idea of taking the lead.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把统治与「领头」联系起来。

items.example: A monarkhes held the office by birth.
items.exampleCN: 唯一统治者凭出生取得职位。

items.example: The suffix turns the ruler into the system of rule.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把统治者转为统治制度。

items.example: The monarch opened the session.
items.exampleCN: 君主为会议开幕。

items.example: The monarchy survived two republics.
items.exampleCN: 这个君主国挺过了两个共和国时期。

items.example: The suffix built monarchic from monarch.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 monarch 构成 monarchic。

items.example: The monarchic title passed to the eldest son.
items.exampleCN: 君主称号传给了长子。

items.example: The monarchist opposed the referendum.
items.exampleCN: 这位君主主义者反对公投。

items.example: The monastery stood above the valley.
items.exampleCN: 僧院坐落在山谷之上。
